evidence: Receiving DO2 fell from 10.38 mg/L at 50.0h to 1.80 mg/L at 50.2h and stayed 1.24–1.90 mg/L through 52.0h — below the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Receiving P assays: 1.09 g/L @36h, 3.04 g/L @48h — mid-growth, matching source trajectory to ~8 g/L peak at 72h
Physical forward model (source-calibrated): estimated transfer multiplier ≈0.40 at h≈50, indicating an oxygen-transfer capacity loss event

Model comparison: strong_feed_reduction gives min DO 0.87 mg/L, post-decision deficit 7.95 mg·h/L, product mass 194.0 kg — best across all actions; keep yields 0.80/8.40/193.9; increase_air 0.71/12.3; combined 0.77/10.6
Model sensitivity: 0/5 feasible members for every action, with strong_feed_reduction min-DO range 0.45–1.29 mg/L
submission.rationale: The receiving batch suffered a step DO2 collapse at ~50.2 h (10.4 → 1.2–1.9 mg/L), violating the 2.0 mg/L oxygen minimum while product was still in strong growth (3.04 g/L at 48h, on track toward the source-like ~8 g/L peak). A stop would forfeit all counted production. The nominal source-calibrated model attributes the deficit primarily to an oxygen-transfer capacity loss (multiplier ≈0.4), so supply-side increases (+15% air) cannot restore feasibility and even extend below-limit exposure. Demand-side reduction is the only lever that mitigates the deficit, and the strongest bounded feed cut (0.6×) performs best: lowest post-decision oxygen deficit (7.95 vs 8.40 mg·h/L under keep), highest predicted minimum DO, and the highest retained product mass (~194 kg). I therefore recommend strong_feed_reduction. Caveat: the model is imperfect and source-calibrated, not the hidden truth; its sensitivity analysis shows no action fully restores DO above 2.0 mg/L, so close monitoring and escalation (equipment transfer-capacity investigation) remain warranted.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated, not the hidden receiving realization; predicted DO2 remains below the 2.0 mg/L limit for all actions (0/5 feasible sensitivity members), so the intervention mitigates but may not eliminate the constraint violation. Delayed assay information (next P point at ~52h available at 56h) could revise trajectory estimates. The true root cause (transfer-capacity loss vs. contamination event) is inferred from the DO2 step at 50.2h and is not directly observed.

evidence: Receiving DO2 sensor: 50.0 h = 10.38 mg/L, 50.2 h = 1.80 mg/L, 52.0 h = 1.26 mg/L (sustained below minimum_do_mg_l = 2.0)
Source batches show no analogous crash at ~50 h (source-1: 10.92 mg/L at 51.0 h; source-2: 11.10; source-3: 11.47), indicating a receiving-specific oxygen deficit
Receiving P assay at 48 h (available 52 h) = 3.04 g/L, comparable to sources (3.02–3.06 g/L), so productivity is on track and worth preserving
Allowed action bounds: combined = [feed 0.8, air 1.15]; reduce_feed = [0.8, 1.0]; increase_air = [1.0, 1.15]
submission.rationale: The receiving tank is in an active oxygen-constraint violation: DO2 crashed abruptly from ~10.4 mg/L at 50.0 h to ~1.8 mg/L at 50.2 h and remained at 1.2–1.8 mg/L through the decision time of 52.0 h, well below the 2.0 mg/L minimum. This is a receiving-specific event — all three source batches show DO2 around 10–11 mg/L in the same window, so it is not a source-driven input pattern. The process is mid-production (receiving P = 3.04 g/L at 48 h, matching sources), so a stop would forfeit counted production and a strong feed cut (40%) would sacrifice biomass/product trajectory unnecessarily. A 15% air increase alone is uncertain to recover DO2 from ~1.3 to >2.0 given the unknown magnitude of the demand/transfer deficit; a feed reduction alone leaves the transfer deficit unaddressed. The combined intervention (20% feed reduction + 15% air increase) attacks both oxygen demand and supply with a bounded, moderate feed penalty, giving the best chance of restoring DO2 above 2.0 mg/L while retaining product mass. No extra assay was requested: the crisis signal is the online DO2 sensor, and the 4-hour assay turnaround would run the process under KEEP while already in violation.
submission.uncertainty: The hidden receiving kinetics are unknown, so it is uncertain whether +15% air with a 20% demand reduction is sufficient to lift DO2 from ~1.3 mg/L above 2.0 mg/L; if the underlying deficit is large (e.g., a much lower kLa in the receiving vessel), strong_feed_reduction (0.6 feed) might have been necessary. Conversely, if the DO2 drop were a transient sensor artifact, a milder increase_air-only action would have sufficed and avoided any feed penalty. Feed reduction also carries a risk of reduced product formation over the remaining run, though the 20% cut is bounded and reversible in review.
